original.reason: It correctly counts q^2 residue classes, but it asserts without justification that q≡3 (mod 4) makes q irreducible in Z[i], and also does not justify why the resulting finite integral domain is a field.

judgment.reason: It rigorously establishes irreducibility using norms, uses Euclidean-domain facts to obtain primality, and proves that a finite integral domain is a field.
The norm argument correctly proves irreducibility, and the subsequent prime-ideal and finite-domain arguments are complete.
It merely asserts the essential fact that q≡3 (mod 4) implies irreducibility in Z[i], without proving or adequately justifying it.
It leaves the key irreducibility claim for q≡3 (mod 4) unsupported; the remaining argument is correct conditional on that claim.
